title: After 12 years of contracting, AI is bringing the magic back
author: Zenity07
selftext:
I've been trying to find the right words for this post without turning it into a wall of text, so I'll try to keep this short.

After several decades of making games (about 15 years full time now, with the last 12 years as a contractor), it's only now with AI that I can actually tackle the projects I've always wanted to make. Some people will want to tell me that this is a bad thing, but after decades of trying and only seeing the video games industry turn to shit, I'm just all out of fucks to give.

Last year I was still convinced that AI couldn't reason and would likely never be suitable for game development (at least not the LLM approach). Boy was I wrong. This last year has changed literally everything, and things have been moving so fast I can't even blame anybody who hasn't quite caught up to it. I probably would still not believe it if I had been too busy to really dive into it myself.

After my last contract I decided to fully commit, started with a few smaller games (I've put some [online](https://wavedash.com/teams/zenity) if you are curious) and now that I am really comfortable with the AI workflow and believe that I have a pretty good idea what can be accomplished with it, I started proper development on my "dream game", the one I've wanted to make for many years (and often tried to start) but never saw a realistic path to getting it done.

So far I've been working on the technical foundations, and most importantly working out an art style and a workflow for building levels, which so far has always been major stumbling blocks for me. The gameplay and characters are still placeholders, but also enough to prove the concept already.

I've asked Claude to make a video illustrating the progress we've made in the first 10 days, and this is the result. The map in the video is entirely made by AI. The workflow for it went something like this:

\* First I developed the art style itself. This actually started by building a custom 3D modeller, but when I settled on this style I realized that I don't even need it to create this toy world look from basic building blocks like wooden blocks, cardboard cutouts, and masking tape.

\* Then I've had Claude clone a few maps and rebuild them using our toolkit to figure out how various layout problems can be solved with it. This also taught us a bunch of lessons for good level design that I've asked it to record.

\* Finally I had Claude build the map based on everything we've learned so far and iterate on it a few times. I didn't directly touch any part of it, but instead built an in-game editor which lets me mark specific spots on the map and place rulers so I can give the AI specific instructions for what I want to change.
